$comment: NEON LINK design tokens — single source of truth for the web UI and the 128x128 device display. Edit this file, then run scripts/gen_design.py. Never hand-edit a generated file.

color.$comment: Web palette. DESIGN_SYSTEM.md 3.1. Dark-first. Neon cyan is the 'system is alive / Link is present' colour; magenta is reserved for wireless/BLE personality. Do not rainbow the UI.

neon.use: Primary accent — Link active, focus, key actions

contrast.$comment: Pairs asserted by scripts/check_contrast.py. 'min' is the required WCAG ratio: 4.5 for body text, 3.0 for large text (>=24px or >=19px bold) and UI component boundaries.

pairs.note: hairline only — must be visible, not loud

space.$comment: 4px base grid. The device works on the same grid at 1:1 pixels, which is why the two surfaces share proportions.

radius.$comment: Radius 0 everywhere. Hard corners are the structural rule carried over from the panel theme study — the module is a machined face, not a rounded app.

border.$comment: 1px for dividers inside a surface, 2px for the outer edge of an interactive element.

touch.$comment: Minimum interactive target in px. The web UI is used from a phone next to a rack in a dim room.

type.$comment: System UI stack + a digits-only subsetted mono for tabular figures. Nothing is fetched from a CDN: the device serves this page from its own access point with no internet.

family.ui: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
family.mono: 'NEON Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, 'JetBrains Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

tracking.$comment: 'token' is the tracking for status words shared with the device (LINK, STOP, AP) — spaced out so they read as machine state, not prose.

motion.$comment: DESIGN_SYSTEM.md 8. Subtle and fast, never decorative. The device gets hard cuts only.

device.$comment: 128x128 1-bit layout constants. Consumed by neon/ui/theme_gen.hpp and by the style-guide simulator so the web page can draw the device's proportions exactly.
device.$hero_note: Glyph width, height and tracking belong to the face itself and live in design/fonts/hero.json — defining them here too would emit two constants for one fact.
device.$confirm_note: Confirmation screen: message lines and the NO/YES boxes. Previously hard-coded in ui_widgets.cpp; moved here when the compact layout needed its own values.
device.$layout_note: Home screen: header 0-12, hero BPM 22-48, unit label 52, status row 66, identity 78, deliberate empty band 88-102 (density rule: a 128x128 display rewards restraint), phase bar 104-120.

device_compact.$comment: 128x64 1-bit layout for native SSD1306/1309 panels (docs/DAISY.md section 4). Shares the 128-wide header band with the layout above — margin, header_text_y, header_rule_y, icon_size, list_gutter, bar_inset and focus_inset stay common constants; everything that re-flows vertically lives here. Rendered into the TOP HALF of the shared 128x128 framebuffer (rows 64-127 stay blank), so a 64-row panel's flush is pages 0-7 verbatim.
device_compact.$dropped_note: unit_y / ident_y = -1: the band does not exist in the 64-row flow. The hero is self-evidently a tempo, and the identity row is dropped with it — screens that show extra identity detail gate on ident_y >= 0.
device_compact.$layout_note: Home screen: header 0-12, hero BPM 15-41, status row 44, phase bar ticks 52-53, bar 54-61, ticks 62-63. Four list rows at the same 12 px pitch as the big layout — the density rule survives the halving; nothing gets a squeezed font.

phase_bar.$comment: The one proportion both surfaces must share exactly (DESIGN_SYSTEM.md open decision 15.4). The web phase bar is the device bar scaled up: same aspect ratio, same inset ratio, same tick treatment.
